metrics.name: mc_quest_player_points
metrics.help: Quest points for an online player, by category. For a skull hunt, category = skulls gives the number of skulls found.

metrics.name: mc_quest_player_tags
metrics.help: Tags added to a player SINCE THEY CONNECTED. Not their lifetime total: the collector doesn't read the database, only what happened while it was watching.

metrics.name: mc_quest_tags_removed_total
metrics.help: Tags removed. A progress reset shows up here.

metrics.name: mc_quest_tags_total
metrics.help: Tags added since startup. For skull hunts, tag = found_<key>: this is THE metric for finds.

collector.name: betonquest
collector.text:
Quest progress, without touching the database.

BetonQuest keeps its state in MySQL, but a `SELECT tag, COUNT(*)` would couple this exporter to a schema it doesn't own, require a JDBC connection, and make TPS depend on a database's health. BetonQuest also emits real Bukkit events — `PlayerTagAddEvent`, `PlayerUpdatePointEvent`, `PlayerJournalAddEvent` — carrying the tag, category, count and profile, so there is nothing to query: listening is enough.

The trade-off: counters reset on server restart, so "how many players have ever found this skull" is not a question this collector can answer — `increase()` over a window, yes; lifetime totals, no. The per-player gauges cover part of that gap: while a player is online, their progress is published as an absolute value, and they can't progress while offline anyway.
